hints: Set up the area integral $\int_{1/4}^4 \left(\frac{5}{2} - x^{1/2} - x^{-1/2}\right) dx$.
walkthrough:
Set up the definite integral for the area enclosed between the upper and lower curves from $x = \frac{1}{4}$ to $x = 4$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_{1/4}^4 \left(\left(\frac{5}{2} - x^{1/2}\right) - x^{-1/2}\right) dx = \int_{1/4}^4 \left(\frac{5}{2} - x^{1/2} - x^{-1/2}\right) dx$$

Integrate each term using the reverse power rule:
$$\text{Area} = \left[ \frac{5}{2}x - \frac{2}{3}x^{3/2} - 2x^{1/2} \right]_{1/4}^4$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = 4$ and lower limit $x = \frac{1}{4}$:
$$F(4) = \frac{5}{2}(4) - \frac{2}{3}(4^{3/2}) - 2(4^{1/2}) = 10 - \frac{2}{3}(8) - 2(2) = 6 - \frac{16}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$$
$$F\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) - \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{1}{8}\right) - 2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{5}{8} - \frac{1}{12} - 1 = \frac{15 - 2 - 24}{24} = -\frac{11}{24}$$

Subtract the lower limit evaluation from the upper limit:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{2}{3} - \left(-\frac{11}{24}\right) = \frac{16}{24} + \frac{11}{24} = \frac{27}{24} = \frac{9}{8} \quad (\text{or } 1.125)$$

hints: Evaluate the gradient at $(1, 1)$ to find normal gradient $m_{\text{normal}} = 2$.
Form the normal equation $y - 1 = 2(x - 1)$ and find its $y$-intercept $p$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the gradient of the curve at $(1, 1)$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1} = -\frac{1}{2}(1)^{-3/2} = -\frac{1}{2}$$

Determine the gradient of the normal line perpendicular to the tangent:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{-1/2} = 2$$

Form the equation of the normal line through $(1, 1)$:
$$y - 1 = 2(x - 1) \implies y = 2x - 1$$

Find the $y$-intercept at $(0, p)$ by setting $x = 0$:
$$p = 2(0) - 1 = -1$$
